next_question: Is direct schema comparison (structural diff of schema definitions, bypassing indirect behavioral/temporal signals entirely) required for reliable drift-vs-noise discrimination, or do fundamentally different signal families (session token validation, field-usage profiling) provide orthogonal discrimination that structural+temporal signals cannot?
why_next: Four single-signal families (Jaccard, TF-IDF, response-time KS, linear ensemble of Jaccard+KS) have now been tested and falsified on the same mock server, all failing for the same root cause: magnitude confound where structural noise patterns produce larger divergence than true drift. The two tested signal families (structural similarity, temporal response) are not complementary — both are confounded by structural complexity magnitude in the same direction. The material next step is to test a fundamentally orthogonal approach: direct schema comparison (schema diff) which measures semantic/structural change directly rather than indirectly via behavioral signals, or session-level behavioral signals (token validation, field-usage profiling) which test a different dimension entirely.

established: Linear Fisher LDA ensemble of (1-Jaccard) and KS D fails all three frozen decision conditions on held-out test split: AUC=0.625, best operating point TP=0.5 FP=0.0 (threshold 0.4603), no point satisfies TP>=0.8 + FP<=0.15. Positive control fails (TP=0.25 on training). (result.json metrics, audit.json recomputed_metrics)

Ensemble weights are inverted: w=[-7.14, -1.33] with intercept 1.14, indicating both features inversely predict drift — higher divergence and KS D associated with noise, not drift. (result.json metrics.ensemble_weights)

Magnitude confound confirmed as root cause: noise patterns (nested_object_variation, null_valued_fields) add 2 fields vs drift patterns (add_field) add 1 field, causing noise to produce larger structural and temporal divergence than true drift. This is now the fourth independent confirmation of the inverted direction across all tested signal families. (result.json observations[8-9], audit.json V_INVERTED_DIRECTION_CONFOUND)

Four single-signal families tested and falsified: Jaccard structural similarity FP=1.0 at all sizes (EXP-GRAPH-34788722106); TF-IDF semantic similarity TP=0.972 FP=1.0 inverted (EXP-GRAPH-35010853847); response-time KS test TP=0.0 FP=0.1875 inverted (EXP-GRAPH-35083040517); linear ensemble AUC=0.625 all conditions fail (this experiment). (all parent handoffs, this result.json)

Fresh copies (identical schemas) have Jaccard=1.0 and KS D ~0.13-0.27, easily distinguishable from both drift and noise. Fresh copy detection is NOT the problem — drift-vs-noise discrimination is. (report.md, parent handoff carry_forward.established)

Mock server produces computation-dependent timing (R²=0.9999, +9.3ms/field) so temporal signals are confounded with structural complexity. Failure is signal-to-noise, not MEASUREMENT_INVALID. (audit.json validity_findings[0])

recommended_action: Design a graph lane experiment testing direct schema comparison (structural diff of schema definitions) as a freshness signal, bypassing indirect behavioral/temporal signals entirely. The approach should diff schema structures (field names, types, nesting, required/optional status) and measure whether the diff magnitude or diff type discriminates drift from noise without the magnitude confound. If direct schema comparison fails, pivot to session-level behavioral signals (token validation, field-usage profiling) which test a fundamentally different dimension. The frozen decision rule should use per-sample features (not aggregated means) with N>=30 per condition to ensure adequate power. The magnitude confound (2-field noise vs 1-field drift) must be controlled for in the experimental design — either by matching noise magnitude to drift magnitude or by measuring magnitude-normalized features.
